findings.title: Phantom file: regressions.json referenced but never defined, created, or written by any component
findings.detail:
The proposer-spec.md (line 29) lists `<repo>/.audits/regressions.json` as a Proposer input for 'Bump priority on repeat bugs'. The audit-broadcast SKILL.md (lines 32, 84) also reads from it. However, this file does not exist in the self-heal pipeline spec (which defines all data files: index.json, closed.json, proposed-rules/), is not listed in README.md's data-files table (line 214-218), is not produced by any script or subagent in the system, and does not exist on disk anywhere.

The self-heal pipeline handles regressions by tagging findings with `status: 'regression'` inside the normal index.json/scan files (self-heal-pipeline.md lines 103-129). There is no separate regressions.json. Two consumer components (proposer-spec, audit-broadcast) reference a file that no producer component creates.

If the Proposer or broadcast skill were implemented as-spec, they would silently skip regression data (best case) or error on missing file (worst case), undermining the regression-priority-boost that is a core ranking feature (score +30 bonus per proposer-spec line 56).
findings.fix_sketch: Decide: either (a) add a regressions.json writer to the self-heal pipeline or audit-scan that materializes regression findings into a separate file, and document it in self-heal-pipeline.md + README.md data-files table, OR (b) update proposer-spec.md and audit-broadcast SKILL.md to read regressions by filtering index.json for `status == 'regression'` instead of expecting a separate file. Option (b) is simpler and consistent with the existing data model.

findings.title: README finding counts are stale: claims '46 open (9C/31I/6CO) across 6 repos' but actual data shows 39 open (6C/28I/5CO) across 5 repos
findings.detail:
README.md line 45 states: '6 repos baselined (IFleet, factory, PhillUp, ~/.claude self-audit, + 2 more) with 46 open findings (9 CRITICAL / 31 IMPORTANT / 6 COSMETIC) as of 2026-05-21.' Verified reality: only 5 repos have .audits/ directories (IFleet, factory, PhillUp, discord-claude-bot, ~/.claude). The actual totals across these 5 repos are 39 open findings (6 CRITICAL / 28 IMPORTANT / 5 COSMETIC).

The '+ 2 more' is vague and unverifiable. The 6th repo does not exist on disk. This isn't a rounding error — it's a 18% overcount on total findings, 50% overcount on CRITICALs (9 claimed vs 6 actual), and a phantom 6th repo.

As a documentation repo whose primary purpose is being the source of truth for the audit system, stale headline numbers erode trust. Anyone reading the README to understand system state gets a materially wrong picture.
findings.fix_sketch: Run `audit-status.sh` across all repos, update the counts on README.md line 45 to match reality. Either identify and baseline the 6th repo or change '6 repos' to '5 repos'. Remove '+ 2 more' — name all repos explicitly.

findings.title: rubric.json field name mismatch: audit-scan.md reads 'version' but actual field is 'rubric_version'
findings.detail:
audit-scan.md line 185 says: `rubric_version = read 'version' field from ~/dev/ai-products/audit-elevation/rubric.json; omit if file missing`. The actual rubric.json has no top-level 'version' key. The field is named 'rubric_version' (line 2). There is also a 'schema_version' (line 3, integer 1) which is different.

Because the instruction says 'omit if file missing' but not 'omit if field missing', an implementation that faithfully follows the spec would attempt `json['version']`, get undefined/KeyError, and either crash or silently produce a null rubric_version in the online_eval_log row. The field would perpetually be empty in the Supabase table, making rubric version tracking useless for drift detection — which is the stated purpose of v2.

This is a load-bearing field name mismatch between the rubric (source of truth, per README line 77) and the consumer (audit-scan command).
findings.fix_sketch: Either rename the field in rubric.json from 'rubric_version' to 'version', or (preferred) update audit-scan.md line 185 to read: `rubric_version = read 'rubric_version' field from ~/dev/ai-products/audit-elevation/rubric.json`.

findings.title: README claims rubric.json is 'schema source-of-truth' for online_eval_log but rubric.json contains no online_eval_log schema
findings.detail:
README.md line 77 states: 'Schema source-of-truth: rubric.json in this repo'. This refers to the online_eval_log Supabase table (22 cols, schema_version=1). However, rubric.json only defines severities, categories, fingerprint_algo, events, and triggers — zero references to online_eval_log, its columns, or its schema.

The actual online_eval_log column definitions live only inside audit-scan.md's embedded curl payload (lines 192-215), where ~17 fields are sent. The '22 cols' claim on README line 76 is unverifiable from any file in this repo — neither rubric.json nor audit-scan.md document 22 columns. The Supabase table itself is the only source of truth, but the repo claims the rubric is.

This means the single source of truth claim is false. If anyone adds a column to the Supabase table or changes the audit-scan payload, there is no canonical schema document in this repo that would need updating.
findings.fix_sketch: Add an 'online_eval_log_schema' section to rubric.json that lists all 22 columns with types and descriptions. Alternatively, create a separate `schemas/online_eval_log.json` and update the README reference. The curl payload in audit-scan.md should derive from this schema, not be the implicit definition.

findings.title: self-heal-pipeline.md recommends flock for closed.json race condition but flock is unavailable on macOS
findings.detail:
self-heal-pipeline.md line 292 documents a race condition when `/audit-fix` and the drafter both write `closed.json` simultaneously, and prescribes: 'Solution: /audit-fix should hold a file lock (flock) when appending.' However, macOS does not ship `flock(1)` — confirmed by `which flock` returning not found.

The lane-scheduler-spec.md (line 70) correctly identifies this problem and uses mkdir-based locking as a workaround. But the self-heal pipeline spec doesn't cross-reference this solution and prescribes a tool that doesn't exist on the target platform.

Since `/audit-fix` and the rule drafter are the primary writers to closed.json, the prescribed race-condition mitigation is non-implementable as written. An executor following this spec would either skip the lock (data loss risk) or waste time trying to find flock on macOS.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the flock recommendation with the mkdir-based locking pattern from lane-lock.sh (already implemented and macOS-compatible). Reference `~/.claude/scripts/lane-lock.sh` as the canonical locking utility, or extract a generic `file-lock.sh` helper that both the lane scripts and audit-fix can source.

findings.title: README lists lane-scheduler.{sh,mjs} but lane-scheduler.sh does not exist
findings.detail:
README.md line 210 documents: 'Lane scheduler | ~/.claude/scripts/lane-scheduler.{sh,mjs} | Observer daemon (opt-in PM2)'. The .mjs file exists, but `lane-scheduler.sh` does not exist on disk. Verified: `ls /Users/Seb/.claude/scripts/lane-scheduler.sh` returns 'No such file or directory'. Only `lane-scheduler.mjs` and `lane-scheduler.pm2.json` exist.

The lane-scheduler-spec.md correctly describes only the `.mjs` file (line 92: 'Node ESM script'). The README's component table is the authoritative inventory for the system — a phantom entry here means anyone trying to locate system components hits a dead reference.
findings.fix_sketch: Change README.md line 210 from `lane-scheduler.{sh,mjs}` to `lane-scheduler.mjs` (and add a separate row for `lane-scheduler.pm2.json` if desired).

findings.title: Proposer watchlist references 3 repos that do not exist on disk
findings.detail:
proposer-spec.md section 2 defines a default watchlist at `~/.omc/proposer-watchlist.json` with 5 repos. Three of these do not exist: `~/dev/ai-products/voice-discovery`, `~/dev/ai-products/spec-template`, `~/dev/weautomatehq.com`. All three return 'No such file or directory'.

The Proposer spec section 6 (Failure modes) covers several error cases but does not address 'watched repo does not exist on disk'. The audit-fingerprint-watcher.sh has this covered (it skips missing dirs), but the Proposer spec has no analogous handling.

When the Proposer is eventually implemented, it would either crash on missing repo paths or silently skip 60% of its input, producing a plan that systematically ignores most of Sebastian's portfolio. The default watchlist should reflect reality.
findings.fix_sketch: Update the default watchlist to include only repos that exist (IFleet, factory). Add PhillUp and discord-claude-bot which have actual .audits/ data. Add a failure mode row for 'watched repo path does not exist' with behavior: skip + warn in DM. The watchlist file at ~/.omc/proposer-watchlist.json is edited by hand (per spec), so the default in the doc should be realistic.

findings.title: ADR-003 references 'eventual-growing-raven.md' — a stale codename that does not exist
findings.detail:
ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 121 (ADR-003 Context section) states: 'The standalone system writes audit findings to `<repo>/.audits/<timestamp>.json` with the schema from `eventual-growing-raven.md` (lines 74-98).' This file does not exist anywhere on disk — it appears to be a Claude-generated session codename from the original build conversation that was never a real file.

The actual schema is defined in plan.md (lines 74-98, which the line numbers match). The reference should point to `plan.md` in this repo, not to a phantom file. An executor trying to look up the canonical finding schema for the IFleet fold-in would hit a dead link on the most important ADR (ADR-003 defines the trace-event schema).
findings.fix_sketch: Replace 'eventual-growing-raven.md (lines 74-98)' with 'plan.md (lines 74-98) in the audit-elevation repo' or with 'rubric.json + plan.md'. The session codename was likely the conversation title during the overnight build — it was never a file.

findings.title: Codex CLI not installed — Phase 2 shipped status is misleading since codex --version fails
findings.detail:
README.md line 36 marks Phase 2 as '✅ shipped (file-level — Codex CLI smoke pending)'. The parenthetical qualifier is honest, but 'shipped' with a checkmark is misleading when `codex --version` fails (not on PATH). The plan.md Phase 2 prerequisites (lines 107-108) explicitly state: 'Install Codex CLI + flat-rate subscription. Confirm codex --version resolves.' This prerequisite is not met.

The codex-review skill exists on disk (~/.claude/skills/codex-review/SKILL.md), so the file-level claim is accurate. But the Tiered review chain in splittasks SKILL.md (lines 218-235) will silently fail or error on any actual PR review because the underlying CLI binary is missing. The fallback behavior (codex unavailable) is only defined in ADR-002 (line 91), which is DRAFT status and describes IFleet pipeline behavior, not the standalone skill's behavior.

This means strict-mode splittasks runs that open audit-fix PRs will hit the codex-review invocation and fail. The system has a shipped reviewer chain with a missing binary underneath.
findings.fix_sketch: Either: (a) install Codex CLI and confirm the smoke test, changing status to truly shipped, OR (b) change the README status to '🟡 file-level only — Codex CLI not installed' and add a graceful fallback to the standalone codex-review SKILL.md for when `codex` is not on PATH (log warning, skip Codex leg, let Claude-only review proceed). The splittasks Tiered chain should also handle codex-unavailable gracefully.

findings.title: Proposer-spec and ADR-005 have conflicting cron time recommendations
findings.detail:
proposer-spec.md D7 (line 129) recommends 03:00 local with rationale 'Sebastian usually starts at 08:00; 5h buffer covers Discord MCP retries.' ADR-005 open questions (ifleet-integration-adrs.md line 249) suggests '6am local? Sebastian wakes ~6:30am. Suggest: 6:15am, gives 15 min for Discord DM to settle.'

These are written by different lanes in the same overnight split (T5 wrote proposer-spec, T1 wrote ADRs) and give contradictory timing recommendations (03:00 vs 06:15). The proposer-spec is the more detailed document and should be canonical, but an executor reading the ADR would get a different answer.

The wake time assumption also differs: proposer-spec says 08:00, ADR-005 says 06:30. This is the kind of inconsistency that two parallel lanes produce when they don't share a single source of truth for operational assumptions.
findings.fix_sketch: Defer to proposer-spec.md D7 as canonical (it is the dedicated spec). Update ADR-005 open question to reference D7 instead of proposing a conflicting time. Remove the 6:15am suggestion or mark it as 'superseded by proposer-spec D7'.

findings.title: watched-repos.txt only covers 2 of 5 audited repos — fingerprint watcher misses 60% of audit data
findings.detail:
~/.claude/audit-watched-repos.txt lists only IFleet and factory. But .audits/ directories with active findings exist in PhillUp, discord-claude-bot, and ~/.claude as well. The fingerprint watcher and rule drafter will never process closures from those 3 repos, meaning repeat-fingerprint detection is blind to 60% of the audit corpus.

This is not a bug per se — the file is documented as manually maintained. But it's an operational gap that undermines the self-heal pipeline's value proposition: if the same bug pattern appears in PhillUp 3 times, no DRAFT rule will ever be proposed because the watcher doesn't scan PhillUp.
findings.fix_sketch: Add the missing repos to the watched list: /Users/Seb/dev/products/PhillUp, /Users/Seb/dev/coordination/discord-claude-bot, /Users/Seb/.claude. Consider adding a periodic reconciliation step to the fingerprint watcher that warns if it finds .audits/ directories not in the watched list.

findings.title: README data-flow diagram shows closed.json in the merge path but closed.json does not exist in any repo
findings.detail:
The README data-flow diagram (lines 156-160) shows a step where merge produces a closure in closed.json. The self-heal-pipeline.md defines closed.json's schema in detail. However, no closed.json file exists in any of the 5 audited repos. This is consistent with the self-heal pipeline being 'scaffolded' (Phase 4 status) not 'shipped', but the data-flow diagram presents it as part of the current working system without qualification.

A reader looking at the diagram would assume the full loop (scan -> fix -> merge -> close -> fingerprint -> draft rule) is operational. In reality, the pipeline stops at 'merge' — the closure-recording and rule-drafting legs have never run against real data (only the synthetic proof in T3-synthetic-proof.md).
findings.fix_sketch: Add a visual qualifier to the diagram — e.g., a dashed-line box or '(Phase 4 — scaffolded, not yet active)' annotation on the closed.json and rule-drafter sections. Alternatively, split the diagram into 'Currently operational' and 'Scaffolded (Phase 4+)' sections.

findings.title: plan.md findings schema shows 'reopened' as a valid status but no component ever sets it
findings.detail:
plan.md line 91 defines the finding status enum as 'open|fixing|verifying|closed|reopened'. The self-heal-pipeline.md adds 'regression' as another status value (line 103). However, no command, agent, or script in the system ever sets status to 'reopened'. The regression-detector creates new findings with status 'regression', not 'reopened'. The 'reopened' status is dead schema — it was designed but never implemented in any consumer or producer.

Minor because it's forward-compatible (adding it later doesn't break anything), but it's an example of speculative schema design that could confuse an executor who tries to implement a 'reopened' code path.
findings.fix_sketch: Either remove 'reopened' from the status enum and note it as a future consideration, or document when a finding would transition to 'reopened' vs 'regression' (the current system uses 'regression' for all recurrences).

findings.title: README Related section uses tilde paths that won't resolve as clickable links
findings.detail:
README.md lines 305-308 use paths like `~/dev/ai-products/IFleet/ROADMAP.md` and `~/.claude/projects/-Users-Seb/memory/` as markdown links. Tilde expansion is a shell feature — these won't resolve in any markdown renderer (GitHub, VS Code, or any browser). They are dead links in every viewing context except being manually pasted into a terminal.

The plan.md and docs/ files use absolute paths or relative paths consistently; the README Related section is the outlier.
findings.fix_sketch: Use absolute paths (/Users/Seb/...) or note that these are local filesystem references not clickable links. For the IFleet ROADMAP, consider using the GitHub URL instead.
